problem_meta.instruction: Inspect the protein with the subsequent sequence and offer a concise description of its properties:
problem_meta.ground_truth: A concise description of the protein with the specified amino acid sequence includes: Transcription factor that is the main target of insulin signaling and regulates metabolic homeostasis in response to oxidative stress. Binds to the insulin response element (IRE) with consensus sequence 5'-TT[G/A]TTTTG-3' and the related Daf-16 family binding element (DBE) with consensus sequence 5'-TT[G/A]TTTAC-3'. Activity suppressed by insulin. Main regulator of redox balance and osteoblast numbers and controls bone mass. Orchestrates the endocrine function of the skeleton in regulating glucose metabolism. Also acts as a key regulator of chondrogenic commitment of skeletal progenitor cells in response to lipid availability: when lipids levels are low, translocates to the nucleus and promotes expression of SOX9, which induces chondrogenic commitment and suppresses fatty acid oxidation. Acts synergistically with ATF4 to suppress osteocalcin/BGLAP activity, increasing glucose levels and triggering glucose intolerance and insulin insensitivity. Also suppresses the transcriptional activity of RUNX2, an upstream activator of osteocalcin/BGLAP. Acts as an inhibitor of glucose sensing in pancreatic beta cells by acting as a transcription repressor and suppressing expression of PDX1. In hepatocytes, promotes gluconeogenesis by acting together with PPARGC1A and CEBPA to activate the expression of genes such as IGFBP1, G6PC1 and PCK1

## Summary

This is **FOXO1 (forkhead box protein O1)**. The 624-amino-acid sequence is an **exact full-length match** to reviewed bovine FOXO1 (UniProt **E1BPQ1**).

FOXO1 is a sequence-specific transcription factor that binds insulin-response and related forkhead DNA elements. It regulates metabolic and stress-response programs, including glucose homeostasis. Its activity and localization are regulated: insulin/AKT signaling can promote its export from the nucleus, while stress-associated signals can favor nuclear accumulation. It shuttles between the **nucleus and cytoplasm**.

The sequence contains a **Forkhead DNA-binding domain** (Pfam PF00250; residues 132–213), plus FOXO-associated KIX-binding and transactivation domains. It also has low-complexity/disordered regions, especially outside the DNA-binding domain.

Sequence-derived estimates: **66.36 kDa**, theoretical **pI 6.60**, and **GRAVY −0.55**. The instability index is **60.14**, a sequence-based estimate—not a direct measurement of protein stability. Functional and localization details above come from the matched reference annotation; they should not be interpreted as experiments performed on this supplied sample.
